tools.name: add_goal
tools.description: Add a goal in the athlete's own words (start with a verb). Mila then plans for it.

tools.name: answer_with_sources
tools.description:
Answer a factual question with sources: a headline of eight words or fewer and one line. Put figures, a list or a table in 'more'. Every number and link must come from this turn's tool results. Name the brand id when it's about one brand. The server draws its logo. Write the card's one-sentence lead-in first, then call this tool: the card shows right under those words.

Use when:
- A factual question whose answer rests on sources (web, their accounts, stored facts).
- It's clearer with a figure, list or side-by-side than a paragraph.

Don't use when:
- Small talk or opinion with nothing to cite.
- Nothing reliable was found: say so in words.
- It's about one of their deals, bookings or goals.
- The answer would be a retired score or rate.

headline.description: Eight words or fewer (48 characters at most).

line.description: Fifteen words or fewer (90 characters at most).

brand_name.description: When it is about one brand: its name (the server draws its logo and cover).

list.description: 'more' as 2–4 rows (a date or label, what, the index of its source).

table.description: 'more' as a table of up to 3 columns and 6 rows (opens on a sheet).

sources.description: Only pages from this turn's results.

tools.name: ask_once
tools.description:
Ask one question, once, when the same choice comes up again and no rule covers it. Give two to four short answers, each with the rule it saves. Never ask what a rule already answers. Never offer an answer that sends, posts or pays without a tap. Write the card's one-sentence lead-in first, then call this tool: the card shows right under those words.

Use when:
- The same kind of choice has come up a second time and no rule covers it.
- The answer changes what Mila does from now on.

Don't use when:
- A rule or fact already answers it.
- An option would make something go out without a tap.
- A deal or reply is waiting on them, or a question was already asked in this chat.

context.description: What prompted it, e.g. "2 product-only offers this month".

key.description: A stable snake_case name for the choice, e.g. product_only_offers.

topic.description: Two or three words that start their own answer, e.g. Free-product offers.

brand_names.description: The brands that prompted it, for their logos.

tools.name: ask_quick_question
tools.description: Ask one question only the athlete can answer, with 2–4 short tap answers that cover it (e.g. This month · This quarter · This year). Their tap comes back as their next message. An open question is one plain sentence instead.

tools.name: bookings_get
tools.description: One booking in full: who, what, when, the money (what they receive, held until the session), its status, whether the buyer's checks passed, what the buyer wrote, and which answers are open to them. Shows the booking card.

tools.name: bookings_list
tools.description: Their bookings: view requests (waiting on their answer or on the buyer), upcoming (accepted or paid, not yet happened) or past (done, declined, canceled, refunded). Each has who, what, when, the money and where it stands. Use for "any bookings?", "what's coming up?", "who booked me last month?". Don't use for deals with brands (deals_find).

tools.name: bookings_respond
tools.description: Put one request in front of them to answer, with your suggestion (accept or decline) leading the card. NOTHING happens from this call: the card's Accept and Decline are their taps on the existing booking confirm, and only those answer the buyer or capture the payment. Use when they ask you to accept or decline a request, or ask what you'd do. Don't use for anything but a request waiting for their answer.

suggest.description: What you'd pick. Their tap decides.

tools.name: bookings_waiting
tools.description: Requests waiting for their answer, soonest deadline first, each shown as a booking card with Accept and Decline (their tap). Use for "anything I need to answer?" about bookings.

tools.name: brand_get
tools.description: What Nomila's research says about the brand behind a deal: category, what it does, its audience, its sports and athletes. Confirmed research only: when the research isn't confirmed to be this company it returns why, and you say you can't judge the fit yet. Use for "who are they?" or before a Fit line. Pass deal_id (preferred) or brand_name.

tools.name: bring_back_goal
tools.description: Bring a set-aside goal back to active. Only when the athlete asks.

tools.name: change_goal
tools.description: Change one of the athlete's goals: its words, its horizon (now = this month, next = this season, later = the year ahead) or its game plan. ONLY when the athlete asked for this change in this conversation; otherwise use suggest_goal. A game plan the athlete writes becomes theirs.

tools.name: check_camera_roll
tools.description: Show a one-tap card that opens a review of the athlete's phone camera roll, so they can add new photos or videos to their library: their phone makes small previews, Nomila scores them, and they pick what to import. Use when: they want to add recent photos or clips; a post of theirs needs a photo or clip they don't have in their library yet (pass for_post with that post action's id); they mention something they shot recently that would make a good post. Don't use: to find something already in their library (media_search does that); to upload or post anything for them; when they have just closed a review; more than once in a conversation. Nomila cannot see their camera roll. Never say you looked at, found or chose any photo or video: say the card opens the review on their phone.

kind.description: What to look at: photos, videos or all (default all). Use videos when the need is a clip.

since.description: How far back: last_review (everything new since their last review, the default), 7d or 30d.

for_post.description: A post action's id, when the review is for one post that needs media. The pick then goes straight into that post's kit.

why.description: One short line on why now, in plain words, for the card.

tools.name: cite_facts
tools.description: Name the F-keys your answer rests on, once, when the answer states facts about the athlete. Code builds "How I got this" from exactly these (plus any web pages you used). Not for opinion or small talk.

tools.name: correct_fact
tools.description: Offer to correct a fact the athlete says is wrong (name its F-key). It is NOT changed by this call: they see the correction and it is saved only if they tap Save; the old fact's history is kept. If it is new information rather than a correction, use remember_fact; if it is unclear which fact is meant, ask.

fact.description: The F-key of the fact that is wrong.

claim.description: What is right, in the athlete's words.

tools.name: deals_close
tools.description: Close a deal for them, internally, when THEY asked in this conversation to say no to it, drop it or file it: reason not_interested (a real offer they don't want), not_a_deal (spam, mass mail, a scam), expired (the moment passed). It's done at once, as their own action, with Undo on the card; nothing is sent to the brand. polite_no: true also writes a short no for their approval (it still needs their Send). Don't use on your own judgement, for a deal they only hesitated about, or to reply (deals_draft_reply with decline is a no that keeps the deal open).

polite_no.description: Also write a short no for their approval (not sent until they tap Send).

tools.name: deals_draft_reply
tools.description: Write a reply to a deal and show it for their approval: the exact email (from, to, subject, body) with Send, Edit first and Not now. It sends nothing; it goes out only if they tap Send. intent: one of the intents deals_get lists for this deal (another returns an error naming the allowed ones). term_asks: the terms they want in the reply, each a term and their number (fee in dollars; usage, paid usage (whitelisting) and exclusivity in months, 0 = none; approval rounds; payment days; logistics hours; commission percent) or yes / no. Only numbers they said in this conversation; a fee only with counter, share_rate or propose_paid. tone: friendly (default) or professional. Use when they ask for a reply or say yes to your suggestion of one. Don't use to send, to answer a booking, or when a reply to this deal is already waiting (deals_waiting).

number.description: Their number for this term, in its unit.

yes.description: For yes / no terms (posting required, school disclosure, travel covered).

tools.name: deals_find
tools.description: List their deals in the board's own order (their money and their move first). Filters: needs_you (their move), in_motion (under way, waiting on nobody urgent), waiting_on_them (the brand owes a reply), closed (done, declined, expired, filed), all. Narrow with brand (part of the name) and from / to (YYYY-MM-DD, by last activity or the day it closed). Each row has the Money line, whose move it is and the next step. Shows the first few as deal cards. Use for: "what needs me?", "anything new?", "what's waiting on brands?", "what did I do with <brand> last spring?" (closed or all, with brand and dates). Don't use: for one deal you already have the id of (deals_get), or for their tap queue (deals_waiting).

tools.name: deals_get
tools.description: One deal in full: the brand, the type, the four-line read (Money, Fit, Risk, Goal, each with its source), what they asked, the latest offer, whose move it is, the next step, what's not known yet, the reply intents this type allows, and whether a reply can go out from the app. Shows the deal card. Use before you judge a deal ("is it worth it?"), before any reply, and when OPENED FROM names a deal. Errors: not_found (check the id with deals_find), not_yours (never one of theirs), closed (call again with include_closed: true to read it as history).

deal_id.description: The deal's id (from deals_find, or OPENED FROM deal <id>).

include_closed.description: Read a closed deal as history.

tools.name: deals_mark
tools.description: Ask them to confirm a change to a deal's stage: signed (the contract is signed), completed (an agreed deal is done), reopen (bring back one they set aside). NOT done by this call: they see a card and it happens only if they tap. Use when they tell you it's signed, done, or that they want one back.

tools.name: deals_open
tools.description: Show a tap-to-open card for a deal (pass deal_id), their deals board (board), or their closed and past deals (closed). Use when they'd rather see it in the app, or after you answered and they want to act there.

tools.name: deals_terms
tools.description: The deal's term sheet, row by row: each term and what they stated, plus the terms that matter for this type and aren't stated yet. Use when they ask about usage, exclusivity, payment, deliverables or what to push on, or before a counter. Don't use for the headline money (deals_get has it).

tools.name: deals_waiting
tools.description: Their queue: replies and ask-for-terms messages that are written and waiting for their tap. Shows the waiting card. Use for "what's waiting for me?" or before drafting something that may already be waiting. Nothing in it has been sent.

tools.name: documents_edit
tools.description: Change one thing on a private document, saved at once (nothing goes out, free): pick_line (another stored option for a line: option is its index from documents_status pages), write_line (new words you write for a line: text, under 240 characters), next_photo (the next-best of their own photos on that page; not for the brand book). document: brand_book | public_page | pitch (pitch needs brand); page and slot from documents_status with detail: pages. Use when they ask to change a line, the tone of a line, or a photo. Prefer pick_line when a stored option already says what they want. Don't use to rewrite a whole document (documents_make). A written line uses only what the page, CONTEXT or they say: never a new fact, number or partner. Example: "make the cover of my pitch warmer" → documents_status (pitch, brand, detail: pages), then documents_edit write_line on the cover's line — not documents_make.

brand.description: Part of the brand's name (document: pitch only).

page.description: The page's id from documents_status (detail: pages).

text.description: write_line: the new words, from what the page, CONTEXT or they say.

tools.name: documents_make
tools.description: Build or rebuild one whole document in the background: a pitch for one of their brands, the public page, or the brand book. Shows a progress card; they can leave, and you come back in this chat when it's ready. Nothing goes out. Costs Nomila about 20 cents for a pitch or the public page, a few cents for the brand book; a document already building is joined, never paid twice. document: brand_book | public_page | pitch (pitch needs brand). angles: up to 3 angles they want the pitch to lead with, in their words (pitch only). Use when they ask for a new pitch ("make me a pitch for <brand>"), a fresh one, or to rewrite the brand book. Don't use to change one line or photo (documents_edit), to share (documents_share), or for a brand the result says isn't confirmed or researched. Errors: brand_not_confirmed, no_research, not_found (not one of their brands), daily_limit, feature_off — each says what to do next.

brand.description: Part of the brand's name (document: pitch only).

angles.description: Up to 3 angles they want a pitch to lead with, in their words.

tools.name: documents_share
tools.description: Get a document ready to go out, for their tap: a live link to their pitch for one brand (document: pitch, brand), or publishing their public page (document: public_page). NOT done by this call: they see a card with Approve and Not now, and it happens only if they tap. Free. Use when they ask to share, send or publish. Example: "send my pitch to <brand>" → documents_share (pitch, brand); you never email the brand yourself. Don't use on your own initiative, for the brand book (it is private), or for a pitch that isn't built yet (documents_make first). After it, say it's waiting for their tap.

brand.description: Part of the brand's name (document: pitch only).

tools.name: documents_status
tools.description: Where their documents stand: the brand book, the public page and each pitch — built or not, building, last updated, shared and opened, published — plus brands a pitch could be made for now. With detail: pages, one document's pages and the lines that can change (each line's slot, its text and its stored options). Free. Shows a card for each document it reports. document: all | brand_book | public_page | pitch (pitch needs brand: part of the brand's name). Use for "what documents do I have?", "is my pitch for <brand> ready?", and before documents_edit (detail: pages). Don't use for their M.I.A., deals or goals, and don't ask for pages just to answer a status question.

brand.description: Part of the brand's name (document: pitch only).

detail.description: pages: one document's pages and the lines that can change (not with all).

page.description: With detail: pages, only this page (its id).

tools.name: drop_goal
tools.description: Drop one of the athlete's goals. Its history is kept and Mila will not suggest it again for 90 days. Only when the athlete asks.

tools.name: find_music
tools.description:
Find music for one post from Nomila's cleared music catalogue. Returns up to 3 tracks, best first, each with a one-line reason, its licence and the credit line the post must carry (null when none is owed).
Use when: a post (reel or story) needs a soundtrack, or the athlete asks for different music.
Don't use: for a still photo or carousel post (they carry no music); to look up a song by name or artist (the catalogue is not searchable by title, and popular songs are not in it); for a trending or platform sound (she adds those in Instagram or TikTok when she posts; they cannot go in the file); to check licences of music the athlete supplied.
use: "brand" for any post made for or with a brand partner — only brand-safe tracks are returned; "personal" for her own content.
min_length_sec: the cut's length; a shorter track that does not loop is ranked down.
If a credit is returned for the track that is used, the post's caption must include it (the post kit adds it and keeps it there).
content_id_registered true: a YouTube upload using it may be claimed (released on dispute once the credit is in the video description); prefer another track when one fits as well.
Example: a 20-second hype reel of a game winner for her own account → mood "hype", use "personal", energy "high", min_length_sec 20.

use.description: brand = for or with a brand partner (brand-safe tracks only); personal = her own content.

energy.description: How much drive the music should have.

theme.description: The kind of video, when it is one of these.

brand_safe_only.description: Personal posts only: also restrict to brand-safe tracks (always on for brand use).

tools.name: health_check
tools.description: Reports whether the agent harness is working. Returns { status, ok, contract, skills, tools }. No arguments.

tools.name: ideas_suggest
tools.description:
Offer post ideas from the athlete's idea bank by their ids (one to five), when they ask what to make or a moment of theirs is close. In your text, mention only the first idea and why it fits. Never invent an idea outside the bank. Write the card's one-sentence lead-in first, then call this tool: the card shows right under those words.

Use when:
- They ask what to post, or one of their moments is close and the bank has live ideas.
- 2–5 live ideas → carousel; 1 → single card.

Don't use when:
- They already said what to make: go to Studio.
- A care moment, or the pillar is paused after "Don't suggest".
- It's a brand deliverable: use the Deal card.
- Ideas were already shown in this chat today.

idea_ids.description: Idea-bank ids, best first. Leave out to show the freshest live ideas.

tools.name: keep_goal
tools.description: Keep a goal Mila recommended (decision_id from list_goals): it becomes the athlete's goal. Pass text only when the athlete reworded it. Use only when the athlete says to keep it.

text.description: The athlete's own wording, when they changed it.

tools.name: list_goals
tools.description: The athlete's goals: active ones with their game plan and this week's actions, set-aside ones, and the goals Mila recommends (each with its decision_id, to keep). Also the next dated events and the biggest risk and upside. No arguments.

tools.name: media_search
tools.description: Search the athlete's own photo and video library (their posts, uploads and Studio output) by what is in the picture, and return the best matches with what Nomila already saw in each: a description, the shot type, the brands visible, whether it is brand safe, whether they are in it, the quality, the curator's keep-or-edit note, and for a clip its shot count and what is said. Use when: they ask which photo or clip to use for a brand, a post or a pitch; they want to find something they already have ("the one from the final", "my clip at the beach"). Don't use: to add new photos from their phone (check_camera_roll); for how posts performed (posts_performance). They cannot see the results from this call: describe a pick by what is in it and when it was posted, never by its id. Never say a photo was posted, sent or changed.
tools.statusLine: Looking through your photos and videos…

query.description: What to look for, in plain words: the moment, the setting, the look or the use ("celebrating with the team", "clean portrait for a skincare brand").

posted_after.description: Only things posted or uploaded on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

posted_before.description: Only things posted or uploaded on or before this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

brand.description: Only shots where this brand is visible.

brand_safe_only.description: true: leave out anything not marked brand safe. Use it when the pick is for a brand.

has_people.description: true: someone is in the shot; false: nobody is (a product or place shot).

detail.description: concise (default) or detailed (adds the setting, the vibe, the curator's reason and a clip's first shots).

tools.name: money_summary
tools.description: The athlete's money in Nomila, read only: what they earned (paid out to them, and paid by a brand directly) this month and this year, what is coming (held on the platform until delivery or confirmation), deposits brands put down, refunds, and whether their payout account is set up. Each line has the brand or booking it came from. Use when: they ask how much they have earned, what they are owed, when they get paid, or whether a payment came in. Don't use: to pay, invoice, refund or move money (nothing moves from chat); for what a deal is worth before it is signed (deals_get). Amounts are exactly as recorded; never add money that is not on record.

period.description: this_month or this_year (default): which paid lines are listed. The totals for both are always given.

limit.description: How many lines per list (1–10, default 3).

detail.description: concise (default) or detailed (adds the holds and refunds lists).

tools.name: offer_capability
tools.description:
Offer one capability from the registry, by key, when the athlete's words or a signal show they'd want it. The server decides whether it may be offered and writes all the words. A yes in words is not a yes: show the card. Write the card's one-sentence lead-in first, then call this tool: the card shows right under those words.

Use when:
- They ask for something CAN DO NOW lists as off and offerable: offer it, never say you can do it.
- An offer signal fires and the capability is available, not core, and unset or past its cooldown.
- Everything it needs is connected.
- They say "yes, turn it on" in words: the card still appears, because a yes has to be a tap.

Don't use when:
- It's core (research, score, deal detection).
- It needs an account they haven't connected: Connect card first.
- They declined it, it's in cooldown, or another offer appeared in the last 24 h.

key.description:
The registry key of what they want. Match their words to what it does:
- post_ideas: Post ideas each week. Post ideas from the new photos and videos you share.
- draft_replies: Draft replies to brands. A first reply written for you when a brand deal arrives.
- voice_send: Send ordinary replies by voice. Send ordinary replies by voice after Mila reads them back.
- auto_archive: Set aside deals that went quiet. Deals nobody worked on for 45 days move out of your list, with Undo.
- moments_scan: Moments worth a post. Mila checks public news about you each week for moments worth a post.
- pitch_deck: Pitch card. A one-page pitch for a brand you want to work with, ready for you to check.
- brand_book: Brand book. Your story and your numbers in one book, ready for you to check.
- plan_refresh: Your plan, refreshed weekly. Mila rebuilds your plan each week and before dated events.
- post_took_off: Tell you when a post takes off. Mila messages you when a post does far better than your usual.
- profile_refresh: Research refreshed monthly. Mila looks up new public sources about you about once a month.
- bookings: Bookings for lessons and camps. Booking requests from your page come to you. You accept or decline each one.

account_ref.description: The connected account it would use, when it rests on one. Leave it out to use their connected account.

tools.name: offer_connection
tools.description: Show a connect card for one account when connecting it would directly sharpen the answer the athlete just asked for and CONNECTED says it can be offered now. Give the reason for THIS question. At most once a conversation.

why.description: One reason, specific to what they just asked.

tools.name: open_screen
tools.description: Show a tap-to-open card for one app screen when the athlete would be better served there: home, goals, goal (pass goal_id), me, scouting (optionally a section: mia, working_for_you, room_to_grow, brands, defines), knows (What Nomila knows). Nothing else can be opened.

goal_id.description: For screen goal: the goal's G-id.

tools.name: posts_performance
tools.description: How the athlete's own posts and accounts are doing, from their connected accounts: recent posts with their likes, comments, reach, saves, shares and views, each against their usual on that platform; each account's followers and engagement now against the start of the window; and what works for them (the patterns their posts show, each marked as leading or an early sign). Use when: they ask how a post or their recent posts did, whether they are growing, or what is working. Don't use: for another athlete's numbers (never available); for what to post next (answer from this, CONTEXT and the plan). Numbers are only what the accounts reported: never round them up or estimate a missing one. With no connected account there is nothing to read: say so and offer the connection.

view.description: overview (default: the accounts, the latest posts and the top patterns), recent_posts, accounts or what_works.

detail.description: concise (default) or detailed (adds each post's caption start and the account's top audience).

tools.name: read_scouting
tools.description: The Scouting report in detail: the M.I.A. read (score, preliminary, confidence), every note on what is working for the athlete, room to grow and what is not on record yet (each with its dimension), their brands (current, past, unclear) and conflicts. Use when they ask why their M.I.A. is what it is, what holds them back, or about their partners, and CONTEXT is not enough.

tools.name: recall_facts
tools.description: Facts about the athlete beyond the CONTEXT block, filtered: `query` (words to match in the subject, claim or topic), `topic` (e.g. sponsor, career, media), `subject_kind`. Each fact comes back with a key you can cite. Use only when CONTEXT does not hold what the answer needs; never page through everything.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. a brand or event name.

topic.description: A research topic: career, sponsor, media, honours, academics, interests, upcoming …

tools.name: refresh_plan
tools.description: Ask for a fresh plan ("plan my week"): recommended goals, game plans, this week's actions and their post kits are rewritten in the background, within the plan's weekly limits. Optionally about one goal. Started: say you're on it and that you'll tell them here when it's done (a progress card shows; they can leave). Refused: say why from the facts it returns, in the same turn.

tools.name: refresh_research
tools.description: Look the athlete up on the public web again and update what Nomila knows about them: a background research run (official team and school pages, Wikidata, a web search) whose checked, sourced facts are added to their record, then their M.I.A. score is re-read. Use it when the athlete asks you to look them up again, says what Nomila knows is out of date or missing (a new team, a new partner or sponsor, recent results, upcoming events), or has just corrected their facts and wants a fresh look. Do not use it to answer a question the facts you already have can answer (use recall_facts), to research another person, a brand or a deal, or to fetch a page they sent you; do not call it twice in one conversation. topics narrows the search: identity (confirm who they are), results_honours, partners, media, upcoming, or all (the default). Returns status started (say you're on it and that new facts will show in What Nomila knows within a few minutes; they can leave), already_running (one is in progress), or a refusal with its reason: rate_limited or daily_budget with next_allowed_at (say when they can ask again), no_anchor (Nomila needs their name and sport first).

topics.description: What to look for. Omit (or all) for everything; identity only confirms who they are.

tools.name: remember_fact
tools.description: Offer to save one durable thing the athlete told you about themselves or their business (a result, a new partner and its dates, a team move, an event, a plan). It is NOT saved by this call: the athlete sees "Want me to save that?" and it is saved only if they tap Save. An event (a game, a meet, a launch) needs the date they said: if they did not say when, ask them before you call this. Set game true when they say it is a game, match or competition they play in. Never contact details, addresses, other people's private details or children's names.

subject_name.description: Who or what it is about (the athlete's own name for a fact about them).

claim.description: One sentence, in the athlete's own words where you can.

date.description: When it was true or happens, YYYY-MM-DD. For an event (subject_kind event) this is required: the date they said, never today's by default; if they did not say when, ask them first.

game.description: subject_kind event only: true when they said it is a game, match or competition they play in.

type.description: Leave unset: something the athlete told you is 'said'.

tools.name: remember_preference
tools.description: Offer to save how the athlete wants things done, what to stay away from, a standing rule, or a name never to use ("Never use: Name"). Only what they TOLD you, never a pattern you noticed. It is NOT saved by this call: they see "Want me to save that?" and it is saved only if they tap Save.

kind.description: voice | style (how they want things done), avoid (what to stay away from, or a never-use name), standing_rule

statement.description: In their words. A name never to use is written "Never use: Name".

tools.name: set_aside_goal
tools.description: Set one of the athlete's goals aside for now (it can come back). Its waiting actions are cleared. Only when the athlete asks.

tools.name: share_insight
tools.description:
Show one thing that changed in the athlete's own data. Pass the fact ids and a headline of eight words or fewer. The server draws the chart and sources. Do not use it to answer a factual question, for a single deal, or for anything you cannot source. Write the card's one-sentence lead-in first, then call this tool: the card shows right under those words.

Use when:
- A real change in their own numbers or record that Mila noticed and they didn't ask about.
- They ask for an insight about themselves, what they're missing, or to see it as a card: look up their facts first, then show the strongest one.
- It rests on stored facts or this turn's results, with at least one source.
- It leads somewhere: a goal, a type of brand, a next step.

Don't use when:
- They asked a factual question (how did X do, who, is it legit): use Answer with sources.
- It's about one deal or booking: use that card.
- There's no number or fact behind it: say it in words.
- It was shown in the last 14 days, or it touches a care moment.

headline.description: Eight words or fewer (48 characters at most).

line.description: Fifteen words or fewer (90 characters at most).

figures.description: Up to three figures for 'See more', each as a cited fact states it.

series.description: For change, strength, gap or timing: the values over time, oldest first, each as a cited fact states it.

brand_names.description: For angle brand: the brands involved.

ask.description: What 'Ask Mila' sends as their message.

tools.name: show_waitlist_card
tools.description: Ask the page to show one of the waitlist's own cards under your reply. card is one of: sport (pick what they play), is_this_you (the profile match Nomila found), handles (the accounts research found, with That's me / Not me), score (their M.I.A. score), invite (their share card and link for their team). Use it when they ask to see one of these again or to go to that step ("show me my score", "where do I invite my team"). The page already shows each card at its step by itself, so don't call it for a card that was just shown. Returns shown true (the card is on screen: point to it in one line, don't repeat what it says) or shown false with the reason (say it plainly, e.g. the score is not ready yet). You never answer a card for them: their taps on it are theirs.

card.description: Which card: sport, is_this_you, handles, score or invite.

tools.name: start_research
tools.description: Start the athlete's sign-up research (Nomila reads public pages about them, keeps the facts it can check, then works out their M.I.A. score), or join the research already running. Safe to repeat: it never starts a second run. Sends nothing outside Nomila. Use it only when CONTEXT or waitlist_status says research has not started and their sport is saved. Don't use it when research is running, queued, done or waiting for more detail (it will say so), and never to look anyone else up. Returns outcome started (new), already_running, queued (it starts when there is room today, by tomorrow at the latest), done, or not started with a reason: no_sport (ask them to pick their sport on the sport card), no_name, needs_more (no public trace yet: a team or Instagram helps), or another reason to say plainly.

tools.name: suggest_goal
tools.description: Suggest a goal the athlete did not ask for: it only adds a recommendation they can keep or set aside, and changes nothing they hold. Needs the facts it rests on: their F-keys from CONTEXT or recall_facts.

fact_ids.description: F-keys (or fact ids) the suggestion rests on.

tools.name: waitlist_status
tools.description: Read the athlete's waitlist status from Nomila's records right now: their research (state, what it is doing now, which steps are done), their M.I.A. score (none yet, the quick score or the full score, with its value of 850 and confidence), the Instagram or YouTube accounts research found and whether they confirmed each, how many sourced facts were found, and their spot on the list. Free, reads only. Use it before you say anything about their progress that CONTEXT does not already state, or when they ask how it is going, how long it takes, or what you found. Don't use it to guess what comes next: say only what it returns, and when a step is still running, say so.

tools.name: whats_next
tools.description: One dated list of what is coming up for the athlete: brand deliverables due, calls and meetings on their deals, booked sessions, this week's plan actions with their due dates, dated events, and what is waiting on them (a deal or booking to answer, a payout account to set up), soonest first, plus anything overdue. Use when: they ask what is due, what is on this week, what they have coming up, or what to do first. Don't use: for one deal's detail (deals_get) or one booking's (bookings_get); to change a date or a plan (the goal tools). Only dates on record: never invent a deadline.

days.description: How far ahead, in days (1–60, default 7).

detail.description: concise (default) or detailed (adds what each deal waits on and why, and each deliverable's format and progress).
